feature_name: TypeScript No Unnecessary Type Conversion Rule
description: Implement a TypeScript-specific lint rule that detects and flags unnecessary type conversions in TypeScript code. The rule should identify cases where developers are explicitly converting values to types they already have, such as using `String(x)` when `x` is already a string, or `Number(y)` when `y` is already a number. This rule will help developers write cleaner, more efficient TypeScript code by eliminating redundant type conversions.
functional_requirements: Detect unnecessary conversions using built-in constructors like String(), Number(), Boolean(), BigInt(), and Symbol()
Check type conversions in both JavaScript and TypeScript contexts, with special handling for TypeScript's type system
Support type-aware analysis to accurately determine when a value already has the target type
Provide clear, actionable error messages that explain why the conversion is unnecessary
Include configuration options to customize which conversion types are checked (e.g., enable/check for String, Number, etc.)
Ensure the rule integrates properly with the existing linter infrastructure and test suite
